parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks two traveller-facing layers. Federally, the 2025 passport/visa regime mandates birth-sex markers, refuses cases with document discrepancies, invites fraud-based lifetime ineligibility, and has blocked/confiscated trans travellers' passports; immigration custody documents beatings, sexual abuse and birth-sex treatment of trans men. Locally, from 1 July 2026 a criminal statute makes facility use matching identity a misdemeanour (up to one year) in government buildings AND public-facing private businesses — restaurants, gas stations, venues, hospitals — a universal exposure covering essentially every venue a visitor enters, with a documented arrest and 24 hours held in the men's ward. Litigation is pending but no proven remedy operates; foreign governments now issue travel advisories. No execution pathway or documented above-baseline killing rate.

entry_documents.exposure: Executive order and Feb 2025 foreign-ministry cable bar X markers and self-selected sex; officers instructed to refuse where documents cast doubt on sex, with fraud-based lifetime ineligibility considered. Trans travellers report confiscated/blocked passports and being stranded; foreign advisories follow.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, limited waivers; ACLU-style suit pending but unresolved.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal can cascade into detention, onward removal, or a fraud allegation if presentation is questioned.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented arrest of a trans woman (trespass, held 24h in men's ward); local law authorises up to one year for first facility offence. Immigration custody records forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans detainees; federal corrections mandate conversion-therapy-style regimes.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass charge requires willful entry plus refusal to leave; habeas and civil suit channels exist; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A facility arrest can move a visitor into birth-sex custody and, for visa issues, into immigration custody with documented abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Universal exposure: criminalisation reaches government buildings and public-facing private businesses (restaurants, gas stations, entertainment venues, hospitals) — the only such law reaching private premises, with steeper penalties; federal orders bar trans people from funded single-sex facilities; ~21 units have school/government bans, 4 criminalise in some circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 units plus capital district have no mapped ban; state challenge filed 30 April 2026; a district judge's 16 June 2026 narrowing is of uncertain status.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal funding orders amplify state bans; no documented remedy has yet halted the local statute.

care_services.exposure: Hospitals are covered as public-facing private businesses, exposing facility use during care; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 patient records; federal orders push defunding of gender-affirming care; emergency-care denial for trans patients not documented but plausible under facility rules.
care_services.protection: Employment-discrimination ruling and hate-crime statute exist as climate signals; prisoner hormone therapy protected by Sept 2024 ruling (resident-facing).
care_services.interaction: Illness or injury forces facility and ward contact, converting a routine medical event into criminal and outing exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official framing is overtly hostile: executive orders label care 'mutilation', direct law-enforcement investigation of 'gender ideology', and a May 2026 counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups as prioritisation targets; cash-reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Rewards memo never uses the phrase as a criterion; strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State hostility lowers police and prosecutorial sympathy when a visitor is reported under the facility law.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans minor using a mismatched facility commits the same offence; March 2026 state law forces disclosure of a trans minor's status to parents within three days (resident-facing but signals climate); pending bills would criminalise facilitating a minor's social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Guardian presence may reduce discretionary confrontation; no documented prosecution of a visiting minor.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family's outing risk rises at hospitals and schools where documentation and facility rules intersect.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific data showing trans killings above the general homicide rate was found; general travel guidance advises checking recent violence reports; 23 units cover gender identity in bias statutes while 37 did not as of 2019.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; employment discrimination prohibited nationally.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin violence data in a hostile-climate jurisdiction is absence of evidence, not evidence of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Suit filed 30 April 2026 and federal challenges remain unresolved; classification of the offence (misdemeanour vs felony) disputed; enforcement record against visitors unknown; oversight machinery has not stopped the policies.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active civil-liberties litigation, legal-aid FAQ on passport rules, functioning courts that have enjoined several federal orders.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists on paper but no documented instance has yet reversed a facility or document exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than Vellandra: that anchor involves exclusion and humiliation without arrest. Here criminal liability up to a year attaches to routine facility use across private premises, plus documented birth-sex custody and federal immigration-detention abuse, so severity is materially greater.

Lower than Ostravia: comparable birth-sex placement and cross-dressing-style criminalisation, but Ostravia's sentences are brief with execution long prohibited and no private-premises reach. This statute's universal coverage of restaurants, venues and hospitals plus federal document refusal at entry makes exposure broader and continuous.

Lower than Kestrel Isles: there the worst outcome is administrative — secondary screening, refused entry, return transport. Here refusal can become a fraud-based lifetime bar, and everyday presence carries custodial exposure through the facility statute, a tier higher on the precedence ladder.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces a continuous, inescapable exposure: from 1 July 2026 nearly every venue entered — restaurants, gas stations, entertainment venues, hospitals, government buildings — is a potential misdemeanour site for using a facility congruent with identity, with a documented arrest precedent and birth-sex ward placement. Layered on top, the federal document regime engineers discovery at entry (marker rules, discrepancy refusals, fraud-based lifetime ineligibility) and channels detainees into custody where abuse of trans people is recorded. Protections exist — pending litigation, a hate-crime statute, 29 states without bans — but no remedy is shown operating against the operative rules, and foreign governments now warn their trans citizens. No execution pathway or documented killing campaign is present, keeping the rating above the extreme floor but firmly in High Risk.
